Where are the answers to 10 questions raised about the Ganges Barrage?
item.description:
India’s experience with the Farakka Barrage shows that it has created such serious problems for both upstream and downstream areas that it has now become a trap. Nazrul Islam and Md Khalequzzaman write about whether Bangladesh could face a similar situation

10 questions about the proposed Ganges Barrage

On 22 August, a discussion was organised by Bangladesh Poribesh Andolon (BAPA) and Bangladesh Environment Network (BEN) at the CIRDAP auditorium in Dhaka regarding the proposed Ganges Barrage.

We raised 10 questions about the barrage: 1. Why such secrecy around this barrage? 2. Will the barrage only use monsoon water in winter? 3. Where is the discussion on the barrage's impact on downstream areas? 4. Why don't Ganges' monsoon flows reach its branches currently? 5. What is the solution to the waterlogging problem in the southwest? 6. How reassured can we be about sediment deposition, flooding, and bank erosion upstream of the barrage? 7. How reliable are the estimated benefits of the barrage upstream of Pangsa? 8. Will this barrage weaken Bangladesh's position on sharing Ganges waters? 9. Why is the planning based on such outdated data? 10. Is it prudent to undertake such a massive budgetary project in the current fragile economic situation?

No satisfactory answers from relevant agencies

The Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) and the organisations that played key roles in formulating this barrage project should have answered these questions on behalf of the government. However, the BWDB rarely shows interest in discussing their projects in public.

BAPA and BEN have organised numerous conferences on the country’s water resources, yet representatives from BWDB, despite being invited, did not attend to explain and validate the government's position. It appeared that they had no representation at the 22nd August discussion either.

Perhaps BWDB currently lacks sufficient internal technical capacity and relies heavily on external research-consulting firms for these tasks. DCC, along with IWFM (Institute of Water Modelling), CEGIS (Centre for Environmental and Geographic Information Services), and a company named Data Ex, undertook the feasibility study and design of the Ganga Barrage Project for BWDB.

It was BWDB's responsibility to ensure that representatives from these organisations attended the discussion and addressed various project questions. BAPA and BEN had also invited these organisations.

It’s challenging to ascertain if they were encouraged by BWDB or responded directly to BAPA and BEN’s invitation, but two representatives from these organisations attended the discussion. One was a former head of CEGIS, now retired, possibly involved in drafting the project before 2016.

Another was from IWFM, playing a crucial role in the project and still active.
The former head of CEGIS claimed that a section of the feasibility study's annexes discusses the barrage's impact on downstream areas. Based on his statement, almost everyone present requested him to share that annex. Follow-up contact for the annex went unanswered.

Earlier, BAPA formally requested the proposed Ganges Barrage's feasibility study and its annexes be shared. Yet, the authorities ignored the request despite the existence of Right to Information (RTI) laws ensuring public access to important information.

The IWFM representative accused us of not thoroughly reading the executive summary of the feasibility report. It’s a serious accusation, no doubt. However, it’s interesting to see how a representative from an organisation that kept their report confidential and didn’t share it, even after a formal request, accuses others of not reading the report.

Effectiveness of foreign experts

To illustrate the quality of the barrage project, the IWFM representative repeatedly mentioned that many foreign experts were involved. Someone familiar with the history of water development efforts in Bangladesh might not be as enthusiastic about foreign experts. In the 822-page book "Water Development in Bangladesh: Past, Present, and Future," Nazrul Islam detailed the history, highlighting that foreign experts were primarily responsible for the tragedies in Bangladesh's water development. Local engineers who silently assisted them also share considerable responsibility.

Therefore, claiming a project is good simply because many foreign experts were involved seems to indicate that many of our engineers still hold a colonial mentality. Interestingly, among the list that the IWFM engineer boasted about, Pakistan was included. The sudden enthusiasm for Pakistan is also intriguing.

The recent example of the Teesta project highlights the challenges foreign experts face in accurately understanding and suggesting solutions for Bangladesh’s river problems. Until recently, almost everyone within BWDB and related consulting firms enthusiastically supported the so-called 'Teesta Master Plan' developed by Chinese experts.

When we criticised the project, they were displeased. Yet, eventually, the Chinese withdrew their initial feasibility study and presented a revised design, which we still found lacking. (For more details, enthusiasts can read our pamphlet Teesta River in Crisis—Which Way Forward?')

Our logical criticism led to the abandonment of the Chinese master plan, and the government is now largely seeking solutions for the Teesta River's problems based on local expertise and the directions we proposed. Against this backdrop, the IWFM engineer's citation of foreign experts to validate their barrage project seems inconsistent and unfortunate.

Almost a month has passed since the 22nd August discussion. Neither the government nor BWDB and the related consulting firms have responded to any of the 10 questions raised. The easiest for them would have been to address the first question (why such secrecy?) by opening barrage-related information, such as the feasibility report and its annexes, to the public. If some parts need to be kept confidential for national interests, they can be redacted. However, it's hard to imagine what those parts could be.

Will the proposed Ganges Barrage be 2nd Farakka?

By keeping project-related information secret, the government is fostering various suspicions. The IWFM representative accused us of not thoroughly reading the executive summary of the project’s feasibility report. Perhaps the reality is the opposite. They might not have expected us to read the summary so diligently that the major deception hidden under the name of the barrage would be exposed.

From the outset, the proponents of this barrage have been explaining to the public that its primary purpose is to store monsoon water for use in winter. But based on the statistics provided in the executive summary, we demonstrated that only 1. 53 per cent of the total monsoon flow of the Ganges could be retained by the barrage.

We further showed that to facilitate a total flow of 698 cubic meters per second in five distributaries (Baral, Ichamati, Hisna-Mathabhanga, Gorai-Madhumati, and Chandana-Barasia) and the Godagari and Bheramara pumping stations during the dry season in Bangladesh, only 209 cubic meters per second (30 per cent) could come from the stored monsoon water. The remaining 489 cubic meters per second (70 per cent) must be sourced from the ongoing flow of the Ganges, which is 1, 295 cubic meters per second.

As a result, due to the barrage, the dry season flow of the Ganges at Pangsa would be shared almost 60: 40; meaning the flow towards Goalando would further decrease by approximately 40 per cent compared to now.

The proposed barrage would be another Farakka. Currently, at Farakka, the Ganga's dry season flow is nearly equally divided between India and Bangladesh. Due to the proposed barrage, the flow of the Ganges downstream of Pangsa would decrease to such an extent, possibly explaining why the executive summary of the feasibility report is so silent on its impact on downstream areas. This possibly also explains why the proponents of the barrage are so displeased because what they might have wanted to hide, we have exposed.

The ball is now in the government's court

The ball is now in the government's court. They must decide whether knowingly constructing another Farakka within the country is wise or whether they should reconsider. During the 22nd August discussion, we proposed five points to tackle the problems in the southwestern regions caused by India’s Farakka barrage. These proposals should be implemented.

In summary, they are: 1. Remove all obstacles in Ganges' branches to increase monsoon flow. 2. Gradually restore connections between the riverbeds and polders through the expansion of TRM (Tidal River Management) programs. 3. Gradually convert coastal embankments into seasonal embankments. 4. Scatter reservoirs across Bangladesh. 5. Ensure fair shares of the Ganges' water from India.

India's experience with Farakka shows that it created severe problems upstream and downstream, becoming a trap. Public sentiment against this trap is growing in India. If, despite this experience, the government decides to proceed with constructing a second Farakka in Bangladesh, it would be genuinely regrettable.

However, we hope that the people of Bangladesh will become aware of the issue and will not be misled by false assurances that the proposed barrage will only store monsoon water for winter use. They should ensure that the same unfortunate outcome from India’s Farakka, leading to a doubled effect from an internal Farakka in Bangladesh, is not repeated.

*Nazrul Islam is Professor at the Asian Growth Research Institute and Former Head of Development Research at the United Nations

*Md Khalequzzaman is Professor at Commonwealth University, Lock Haven, USA

*The opinions expressed here are those of the authors' own.

item.title: Celebrating women entrepreneurs in Bangladesh’s beauty industry
item.description:
Cholo Egiye Jai, a book featuring the stories of 99 entrepreneurs from Bangladesh’s beauty industry, has been published under the planning and editorial direction of Afroza Parvin, Managing Director and Co-Founder of Ujjwala and a prominent beauty expert. The book has been published by Desh Publications.

The book was unveiled at a ceremony held on September 25 at the Notre Dame Club Auditorium in Banani. The event brought together entrepreneurs from the beauty industry, writers, poets, journalists, beauty experts and fashion designers.

The programme opened with a Rabindra Sangeet performed by Antara Ray Chowdhury. Prominent lifestyle journalist Labannya Lipi delivered the welcome address.

“Afroza Parvin has not only brought these entrepreneurs into the spotlight; she has also given them the mental strength to become self-reliant and contribute to society. There was a time when some of them did not even have the courage to speak up at home. Today, they are contributing not only to their families but also to the economy of the country,” she said.
Prominent beauty expert Kaniz Alamas Khan then addressed the gathering, praising the initiative and highlighting the important role women play in Bangladesh’s beauty services sector.

Sangita Ahmed, President of the Bangladesh Women’s Chamber of Commerce, and Farzana Khan, Deputy Managing Director of the SME Foundation, spoke about the various challenges women face in their professional journeys. Both expressed their pride as women in seeing others move forward despite these obstacles.

Sangita Ahmed said she would look forward to the second volume of Cholo Egiye Jai. Farzana Khan, meanwhile, said she would have been happy to be the 100th woman featured in the book.

Three of the entrepreneurs featured in the book—Maruf Munna, Mohsina Munni and Ikra Ahsan Chowdhury—also shared their stories at the event. Each has faced various challenges at different stages of life and built their position by overcoming those obstacles. They expressed their gratitude to Ujjwala and Afroza Parvin for their support and encouragement.

The event also featured remarks by Bangla Academy Award-winning writer Nasima Anis and writer, editor and publisher Nahida Ashrafi.

Nasima Anis said, “Creating women entrepreneurs in the beauty sector is an important initiative in the developing world. Women in our society contribute labour to their families, but that labour often has no financial value. This is a major reason for their vulnerability. When a woman entrepreneur begins to earn, she starts contributing to her family and society. Society is then compelled to recognise her. The work Afroza Parvin has undertaken from her position deserves appreciation.”

Nahida Ashrafi congratulated the entrepreneurs featured in Cholo Egiye Jai, edited by Afroza Parvin.

“When a makeup artist transforms someone, they do not simply enhance their external appearance; they also make them more confident. For this, we can truly respect them from our hearts. In a way, we are all beauticians. Some of us work with words, while others work with makeup,” she said.
She added that awakening this consciousness of beauty and aesthetics could help society move much further forward.

In her vote of thanks, Afroza Parvin spoke about Ujjwala’s journey and its efforts to create opportunities for women beauty professionals. She also spoke about the publication of Cholo Egiye Jai and expressed her gratitude to everyone who contributed to the initiative and attended the event.
Following her remarks, the guests formally unveiled Cholo Egiye Jai.

The event was hosted by prominent and popular actor Afsana Mimi. Beyond her role as presenter, she kept the programme engaging with her lively and thoughtful interactions. She also recited an excerpt from a poem by Shankha Ghosh.

The evening concluded with another musical performance by Antara Ray Chowdhury.

item.title: ‘Roid’ to represent Bangladesh at the Oscars
item.description:
Mejbaur Rahman Sumon’s film ‘Roid’ has been selected as Bangladesh’s official submission in the International Feature Film category of the 99th Academy Awards, popularly known as the Oscars.

The announcement was made at ‘Meet the Press’, held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka, on Sunday morning.

Mohammad Zahirul Islam, president of the Bangladesh Federation of Film Societies (BFFS) and chairman of the Oscar Bangladesh Committee, announced the name of the selected film.

The rise and rise of Nazifa Tushi

A total of five films were submitted for consideration within the 16 September deadline set for Bangladesh’s participation in the 99th Academy Awards.

The submitted films were Redoan Rony’s ‘Domm’, ‘Roid’, Nurul Alam Atique’s ‘Manusher Bagan’, Mohammad Tawqeer Islam’s ‘Delupi’ and Monirul Akash Haque’s ‘The University of Chankharpool’.

‘Manusher Bagan’ later voluntarily withdrew from the competition, leaving four films in contention.

In search of intelligent cinema on a small budget

Following an extensive review, the six-member Oscar Bangladesh Committee unanimously selected ‘Roid’ as Bangladesh’s official submission in the International Feature Film category.

Sajjad Sharif, Shaheen Dil-Riaz, Rashed Zaman, Syed Shahzada Al Karim and Shahreen Akter Sumi are serving as members of the committee.

The BFFS congratulated the film’s director, producer, cast and crew on the selection and expressed hope that it will represent Bangladesh’s film industry and cultural identity on the international stage.

item.title: BITMUN VI to bring over 600 students together for three days of diplomacy and debate
item.description:
Building on the success of its five previous conferences, Bangladesh International Tutorial (BIT) is set to host the sixth session of BITMUN from 1 to 3 October at its 17-bigha Uttara campus. This year, BITMUN VI is expected to bring together more than 600 participants, making it one of the largest school-level Model United Nations conferences in Bangladesh.

For three days, the BIT Uttara campus will transform into a platform for debate, negotiation and diplomacy, where students from different schools will take on the roles of diplomats and representatives of various countries. The conference will feature 14 committees, including the United Nations Security Council and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation.

This year's BITMUN will be held under the motto "Every Move Counts", highlighting the importance of thoughtful decisions, effective communication and collaboration. Through committee sessions and diplomatic negotiations, delegates will have the opportunity to develop skills in public speaking, critical thinking, problem-solving, negotiation, teamwork and leadership.

The theme of BITMUN VI, "Ensuring Peace Through Global Governance Amidst Diverging Interests Conflicting with International Obligations," focuses on the challenges of maintaining peace and international cooperation when countries have different interests and obligations.

The conference will also continue BITMUN's tradition of providing delegates with a complete conference experience. Participants will receive meals throughout the three-day event along with other arrangements, including the conference's signature BITMUN muffler.

The event is being supported by Excellence Consultants as the Title Sponsor, with The Business Standard, Channel 24, Cablegram, The Front Page and Infogram as media partners.

Beyond the formal committee sessions, BITMUN VI will also feature a strong cultural component. The second day will carry the theme "Cha-er Adda", creating an informal space for participants to connect and enjoy the cultural side of the conference. The programme will feature performances by singer Arnob and bands Blue Jeans and Ignite.

With its growing participation and a mix of diplomacy, learning, networking and cultural activities, BITMUN VI aims to bring together students from across the country for an engaging three-day experience centred on global issues and youth leadership.

item.title: Extortion allegation against BNP over attack on Salman Muqtadir’s studio 'sweeping': Salahuddin
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has termed sweeping, content creator Salman Muqtadir's accusation of 'extortion' against the BNP in connection to the attack and vandalism of his studio.

Citing preliminary investigations, he mentioned that Salman Muqtadir appears to have been 'victimised' in the incident.

The Home Minister made these remarks to journalists at the Secretariat today, Sunday.

According to the content creator, on Saturday night, there was an incident of attack and vandalism at Salman Muqtadir's studio located at New Guinea Properties in ECB Square, Dhaka.

He released a video of the vandalism on his verified Facebook page last night and made various comments, including accusations against the BNP of 'extortion'.

Regarding the incident, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that there is a disputed land at the scene, with a conflict between two parties over it. One group attempted to take possession and caused vandalism.

Among the damaged properties was a structure where Salman Muqtadir created content, which was also vandalised. This was shown in the video.

Salahuddin Ahmed noted, "Has the complainant filed any case? He hasn't."

At one point, he mentioned, "It has been heard that nobody asked him (Salman Muqtadir) for extortion money; he supposedly said he would have given if asked."

The Home Minister labeled Salman Muqtadir's claim of the BNP being an extortionist group as sweeping and stated that if Salman files a specific case, the matter will be investigated.

item.title: Intrepid adventurers: On the Road to Mount Elbrus, the final day
item.description:
Ikramul Hasan Shakil is Bangladesh's Everest summiteer with the unique distinction of having conquered both the Great Himalaya Trail and the Sea to Summit challenge. He has set off on a new expedition, this time to Mount Elbrus, the highest peak in Europe, located in Russia's Caucasus range. Sidratul Safayat Daniel brings the story of this challenging expedition in a series of dispatches.

There had been no word from Shakil for several days. During that silence, worry crept in. Perhaps the expedition had been called off, or perhaps something had gone wrong beyond the point of reaching out. When the voice note finally arrived, it carried the news: Shakil had reached the summit of Elbrus! And behind that news lay a thrilling story. Arguably the most difficult and most memorable chapter of the entire expedition.

The day everything fell apart

Since the plan called for a summit push on the night of 24 September, that day was set aside as a rest day. After finishing the previous day's hike and acclimatisation, the team moved up to high camp. The plan was straightforward: depart at 3 am in the early hours of 25 September for the summit push. That was their scheduled, regular summit date.

But the mountain runs on its own terms. From the afternoon onward, the sky's mood began to shift, and by nightfall the weather had turned severe. Conditions were so bad that even stepping out of the tent to reach the bathroom became impossible. Naturally, the 3 am summit push had to be scrapped.

There was still hope, though. They had a reserve day in hand, 26 September. But the forecast brought worse news. After a night and a day of continuous snowfall, the outlook suggested that even if the weather improved, conditions still wouldn't allow a summit push on the night of the 25th leading into the morning of the 26th. Shakil mentioned more than once that weather at high altitude offers no guarantees.

Elbrus and the surrounding Caucasus range are, in fact, known for exactly this kind of sudden weather change. Moist air rising off the Black Sea collides with cold currents from the high mountains and the scene can shift in an instant. This unpredictability has led to tragedy on Elbrus before. In September 2021, a sudden blizzard killed five mountaineers and trapped a group of nineteen. Rescuers worked for hours to bring the survivors down.

Even earlier, in May 2006, seven climbers died on Elbrus after being caught by a sudden turn in the weather. This history explains why guides and expedition agencies remain so cautious when it comes to weather calls.

With that reality in mind, the agency and the guide jointly decided to cancel the expedition. Shakil and Heather repeatedly asked for at least a chance to attempt it. But where the weather itself wasn't permitting it, emotion couldn't outweigh judgment. And they understood that too. Everyone began preparing to descend the following morning.

On the Road to Mount Elbrus: Day One

Waiting for a miracle

That afternoon, as their hopes were dashed. Shakil and Heather sat together and praying. Hoping that even if the odds were less than one per cent, some miracle might still happen. Both of them were deeply disheartened. Their guide couldn't help but notice their disappointment and their longing to at least try.

Toward evening, the guide came back with news. Right after dinner, they could attempt the summit push. The weather was still hostile, visibility was near zero. The snow and wind hadn't let up. There was one condition, if the weather improved as they climbed and they would continue upward. If it worsened, they would turn back immediately. That sliver of a chance was enough to lift Shakil and Heather's spirits.

After dinner, the team held a meeting and a new twist emerged. Two other teams who had been waiting expressed interest in joining them. In the end, the new plan was set, departure at 2 am. Heading for the summit.

Through the night, toward the summit

2 am. The teams left camp in brutal weather. But before they had gone far, the other two teams seeing how severe conditions had become decided to turn back. Only three remained -- Shakil, guide Alexa and Heather.

Climbing high and sleeping low: On the Road to Mount Elbrus, Day Two

Visibility was close to nothing. All around was buffeting wind and snow. Ice building up on their bodies. In such darkness, under such conditions, simply finding the way forward was a battle in itself. But the small team of three didn't give up. After hours of pushing through, they reached the summit of Elbrus at 7:30 am Russian time.

Shakil, Alexa and Heather stood on the summit of Elbrus.

That feeling cannot be put into words. The summit that had seemed impossible just a few hours earlier was now a reality. Standing atop the highest point in Europe, Shakil and Heather proved that sometimes, holding on to even the faintest chance is what changes the entire story.
triumph.

After reaching the summit, Shakil and his team descended safely. Alongside conquering Europe's highest peak, the expedition left Shakil with another lesson that however small a person may feel before nature's decisions on a mountain, patience and belief can  sometimes make the impossible possible.

And so ends this diary of the Mount Elbrus expedition. A series that began with an ordinary early morning journey and closed with an unforgettable triumph.

item.title: TIB seeks accountability over Radda looting, Kishoreganj clash, studio vandalism
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has expressed concern over 3 recent incidents involving the alleged looting and encroachment of the Radda MCH-FP Center, a clash within the local BNP over control of a jalmahal in Kishoreganj, and vandalism at a content creator’s office.
In a statement issued on Sunday, TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said the incidents were not isolated and called for accountability for those involved, along with a nationwide self-purification drive within the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).
He described the looting, vandalism and encroachment at the Radda MCH-FP Center as an example of conduct that could affect the government and the ruling party.
“This nonprofit organization has been providing healthcare to underprivileged and vulnerable mothers and children for 50 years. It has now been demolished before hundreds of people, under the patronage of a reserved-seat Member of Parliament and in the presence of police.
“For its citizens, what kind of example is the ruling party providing? This party received a historic electoral mandate following the violent July uprising that overthrew an authoritarian kleptocracy. What message do its leaders and activists convey to the citizens through such actions?
“The reckless conduct of the previous authoritarian government is still fresh in public memory. In this context, have the BNP’s policymakers ever thought of the consequences of the continuing encroachment and extortion of a large section of the party’s leaders and activists?” he said.
Iftekharuzzaman said that since August 2024, a section of BNP leaders and activists had claimed the mantle of victory following the fall of the Awami League government and had faced widespread allegations of encroachment, extortion and attempts to establish dominance across the country.
“With the political change, many of the party's leaders and activists at different levels, including the grassroots, began acting recklessly. The media, observers and political circles have expressed concern about this issue.
“Immediately after the fall of the Awami League government, extortion and encroachment changed hands, and a section of BNP leaders and activists turned the situation into a free-for-all,” he said.
He said such incidents had occurred at major bus terminals, including Sayedabad, Mohakhali and Gabtoli in Dhaka, as well as in Chattogram, Sylhet and Khulna.
He also referred to alleged encroachment and extortion involving footpaths, markets, water bodies, sand mills, local bazaars, cable and internet connection services, waste collection businesses, and activities at the upazila and union levels.
He said the incidents had frequently resulted in internal conflicts and rivalry that had turned violent, while daily, monthly and one-off extortion had continued.
Moreover, he said a government minister had repeatedly declared that “extortion is not corruption, but a negotiated transaction,” and alleged that the government had taken no action in response.
“As a result, these incidents are occurring more frequently, normalizing extortion and encroachment. This is an ominous sign for the government,” he said.
TIB’s executive director also cited the clash between 2 factions of the local BNP over control of a water body in Kishoreganj and the vandalism of a creative studio.
“These are not isolated incidents. They are simply a continuation of events that have taken place since August 2024. They are sufficient to overshadow all of the government's good deeds and initiatives and to give the public a bad impression.
“The ruling party must honor its anti-corruption electoral commitments and take effective self-purification measures right now. If it does not, it will lose the chance and ability to control such encroachment and extortion in the future, even if it wants to.
“At least, that is what examples from the recent past tell us. The situation may worsen if vested interest groups fail to maintain their control, and it may be too late to take action,” he said.
TIB said that in some cases, such misconduct had embarrassed the party’s senior leadership, prompting organizational measures including expulsion, but that stronger preventive strategies were lacking.
It also said those involved in the alleged abuses of power were directly or indirectly affiliated with the ruling party, leaving law enforcement agencies unable to take effective action.
According to TIB, a culture of arbitrariness, corruption, irregularities and impunity was re-emerging, for which the government would have to bear responsibility on many fronts.
The organization called on the authorities to investigate each of the incidents without delay and ensure that those responsible face exemplary punishment.

item.title: Salahuddin calls Salman Muqtadir’s BNP extortion allegation ‘sweeping’
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said the vandalism at content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio in the capital stemmed from a land dispute, calling his allegation that the BNP is an extortionist party a “sweeping” claim.
“Salman Muqtadir has said nobody demanded extortion money from him. He also said if anyone had asked, he would have paid. So, no specific person has been identified, and then he is saying BNP is an extortionist party. This is a sweeping allegation,” he said while talking to reporters at the Secretariat.
The minister said there was a dispute between two parties over around 35 kathas of land in Manikdi Nampara under Cantonment Police Station, where the incident took place.
“Vandalism occurred amid a conflict over attempts to take possession of the property,” he said.
Referring to Salman Muqtadir’s allegation that vandalism occurred because he had refused to pay extortion money, Salahuddin said no specific person has been identified as demanding money from him. “Besides, he did not file any case over the incident.”
“He can make statements against me—that is democracy and freedom of speech. But my question is whether the gentleman who made the allegation on a Facebook Live has filed any case. He has not,” he said, adding if Salman Muqtadir files a specific case, authorities will investigate it.
The minister said Salman Muktadir was a victim of the vandalism and that authorities have conducted a preliminary inquiry into the incident. “He was victimised in this incident. We have seen that. We conducted a preliminary investigation, but it was very brief. A more detailed investigation is needed,” he said.
Salahuddin said legal proceedings were underway and a case could be filed soon.
According to Salahuddin, the preliminary report said one of the parties involved in the land dispute was a developer, New Gini Properties, while the other was a retired senior military officer.
“According to our preliminary report, a number of people went there at night on behalf of the retired senior military officer to take possession of the land. They vandalised several structures on the premises,” he said.
Among the damaged structures was a tin-shed facility used by Salman Muqtadir for content creation, the minister said.
Police went to the scene after receiving a call through the national emergency helpline 999, he added.
Salahuddin said three people have been arrested in connection with the incident, while police recovered some evidence, including bullet casings and locally made weapons.
The attack took place on Saturday night, when Salman Muqtadir’s studio was also ransacked.
The attackers damaged cameras, furniture, recording equipment and other facilities at Brownfish Studio, where he and his team regularly produce content.
His YouTube Silver and Gold Play Buttons were also reportedly damaged in the vandalism.

item.title: Explainer: How digital banks actually operate
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has taken a major step toward making the banking system more accessible, technology-driven, and inclusive.
As part of fully modernizing the country's financial sector, five institutions have been given preliminary approval to operate digital banks.
Out of 12 applications scrutinized, four new institutions have been issued a 'Letter of Intent' (LoI), according to Bangladesh Bank Spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan.
These institutions are bKash Digital Bank, Bhutan's DK Bank affiliate DK Digital Bank, Banglalink's parent company VEON's Digital Bank, Square Group's Nova Digital Bank, and Robi Axiata's Boost Digital Bank.
Earlier, in October 2023, Nagad and Kori Digital Bank were granted preliminary letters of intent.
Both institutions were directed to build the necessary infrastructure within six months (by April 2024) and apply for a full licence.
Having met the designated conditions, Nagad was granted a full license in June 2024, while Bangladesh Bank renewed Kori Digital Bank's LoI.
A digital bank is a type of banking system that has no conventional physical branches.
These banks conduct their entire operations digitally through websites or mobile applications.
Although this type of bank has no customer service centers or branch offices, it maintains a head office for administrative functions.
Simply put, users can access all banking services online without visiting a bank in person.
Over the last decade and a half, the growth of electronic transactions and payment methods, along with the widespread expansion of Mobile Financial Services (MFS), has significantly increased the adoption of digital financial services.
This shift provided the primary momentum to further accelerate the digital banking framework.
According to a 2025 Bangladesh Bank report, Mobile Financial Services (MFS)—launched in 2011—gained rapid popularity, reaching 54% of the population by 2024.
MFS usage saw particularly significant growth in rural areas, where conventional banking networks remain limited.
Nature and operations of digital banks
A digital bank will function as a public limited company with a paid-up capital of Tk300 crore, maintaining its head office in Bangladesh.
The bank will not operate any of its own branches, sub-branches, agents, or proprietary ATM booths; however, it can utilize virtual cards, QR codes, and existing ATM or MFS networks of other banks for transactions.
Subject to compliance with guidelines issued by Bangladesh Bank, digital banks can leverage existing networks of other conventional banks, mobile financial services, ATMs, CDMs, and CRMs instead of deploying their own agents, ATMs, CDMs, or CRMs.
The bank will not have any branches, sub-branches, windows, agents, or proprietary ATMs, CDMs, or CRMs.
To facilitate transactions for customers, it can issue virtual cards, QR codes, or other advanced tech-driven products.
Accounts in digital banks must be opened by collecting customer identification information entirely afresh.
Digital banks may process inward remittances provided they maintain digital records and comply with the existing regulatory framework.
They can provide financing and loans across all sectors except foreign trade loans and medium-to-large industrial loans.
Customer service for digital banks may be delivered through third parties, subject to Bangladesh Bank approval.
However, no cash deposits or cash withdrawals will be permitted at such customer service centers.
Regarding the formation of the board of directors, digital banks must strictly comply with the "Bank Company Act, 1991" (including its amendments) and all instructions issued by Bangladesh Bank.

item.title: Fuel supply back to normal, says minister Tuku
item.description:
Fuel supply has returned to normal after shortages and accidents caused disruptions in Bangladesh, Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku has said.
“Some time was needed to restore the situation due to fuel shortages and accidents. However, the fuel supply line is now normal,” he told reporters at the Secretariat on Sunday afternoon.
Tuku said fuel can now be brought into the country and supply schedules have been finalised.
“If there are no further accidents, electricity and fuel supplies can be maintained normally in the coming days,” he said.
The minister said the government did not deliberately create the situation and had sought alternative sources to minimise public suffering. He said gas was also imported at higher prices to address the shortage.
Explaining the disruptions, Tuku said the Iran-Israel war affected the Middle East, a major hub for oil and gas supplies, making it difficult to secure alternative sources.
“Even after purchasing fuel, it was not possible to bring it into the country,” he said.

item.title: Home minister: Ex-Cantonment thana OC had links with AL
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said links have been found between former Cantonment Police Station officer-in-charge (OC) Md Rakibul Hasan and Awami League (now facing ban on its activities).
He made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at the Secretariat over recent transfers of OCs at different police stations in Dhaka and the withdrawal of the OC of Shah Ali Police Station.
Asked whether merely transferring police officers could resolve problems, the home minister said transfers are an administrative measure and may be made for negligence of duty or when an officer is found to have links to certain activities.
“But the transfer is not the last step. Departmental proceedings are being taken against them after the transfers,” he said.
Referring to Rakibul Hasan, he said an investigation was conducted into the former Cantonment OC over an incident involving an audio recording that went viral on social media. He said forensic examination was also conducted and that one or two agencies were involved in the investigation.
“A case has been filed against him and departmental proceedings are underway,” Salahuddin said.
He further said charges have also been brought against Rakibul Hasan in connection with a criminal offence, including sedition, and that he has been arrested.
Rakibul Hasan came under scrutiny after an audio recording allegedly featuring his voice spread on social media.
In the recording, he was heard discussing the current situation in the police force, the posting of officers and various internal issues.
He alleged that many senior police officials are becoming involved in BNP politics while grassroots police personnel are not doing so.
He also alleged financial transactions in the appointment of OCs and the use of influential people to secure postings, while claiming that unqualified officers are being given important positions at the expense of competent officials.
In the recording, he also said the police would not be able to prevent ex-prime minister Sheikh Hasina from returning to Bangladesh and expressed dissatisfaction over postings and leadership within the force.
Following an investigation into the audio, Rakibul Hasan was withdrawn from his post and a sedition case was later filed against him.
On Thursday, he was shown arrested in the case and produced before a court, which, after a hearing, granted five days' remand.
The investigation was later transferred to the Detective Branch (DB) .

item.title: The orna shield paradox
item.description:
It is 8 in the morning. I stand in front of the mirror admiring my outfit that I chose to wear at university today,oversized shirts and jeans. But then I sigh as I reach for the hanger and grab my shield. The shield which protects me from piercing stares and street harassment.
My orna .
I drape my orna around my shoulders. Because if I do not, then the stare lasts for a little longer.
That is the morning dilemma of every girl in Dhaka- deciding whether to dress for herself or dress to be unbothered.
Most days, the orna wins.
But it is not just about draping; it is about constantly adjusting, checking if the shield is pinned perfectly, ensuring it is covered enough from the back, and the anxiety of it slipping off in public.
And if one day a girl chooses freedom in how she dresses by leaving off her orna, she becomes the subject of judgmental glares, clicks of tongue and audible sighs of disgust. And it comes from not only men but from women as well.
From random rickshaw pullers and CNG drivers to her family members leaving pointed remarks at the lunch table asking her, “Orna koi?” (Where is your scarf). Quick reminder that she is being watched.
And this public behavior forces her to cross her arms over her chest, walk faster, or hunch her shoulders as a secondary makeshift shield.
Worse still, whenever any woman in our country gets sexually assaulted, a toxic chorus echoes from the gossips on streets to Facebook comments: This happened because she did not wear her orna.
The situation of our country is like this just because girls nowadays do not cover themselves.
This phase thus creates a societal belief where the character of a girl is being linked directly to the two-and-a-half-meter orna and that a girl's safety is her own responsibility rather than the society’s.
A girl not wearing orna is labeled as shameless, rebellious, is asking for attention.
Society starts perceiving her as ‘approachable’ in a negative way, whereas a girl wearing orna is well-mannered and modest.
Modesty ceases to be about behavior and becomes about fabric.
This is exactly when orna transforms from a piece of cloth to a shield against verbal harassment, street harassment, and public objectification.
Because women have learned early on that even if they open up to their family, even their parents, about the public objectification they face on streets, the standard solution offered will be orna.
It is perpetuating a cycle of compliance rather than resistance, and this institutionalized response creates a ringing in our ears about how the choice ends at our doorstep.
This is a form of victim-blaming in advance.
It creates a fear of judgment and a private guilt that keeps victims from seeking help.
But is wearing the orna actually the antidote to all of this?
"I encountered unwanted physical contact while I was moving through the crowds of Gausia New Market, despite wearing an orna with modest clothing." shared 23-year-old Nusrat.
Nabila shared something similar: "I covered myself properly with an orna to feel safe, but I still had to change my route home because of harassment."
The message is clear: No.
These incidents prove that harassment is caused by people's mindset, not by women's clothing.
The core message here is that we must build a society where women are respected for who they are, not judged by what they wear. Wearing an orna should be a personal choice, not an obligation.
It should move from being "just coverage" to being style and identity.
In Dhaka, we're already witnessing a cultural shift -- the orna being styled as a fashion statement and working into fusion wear while still holding onto its cultural significance.
Accelerating that shift, away from forced coverage and toward personal identity, is essential if we want to build a genuinely safe society for the women of Bangladesh.
Tanusree Dhar is a student writer interested in social issues, youth, gender, and voices and experiences that deserve to be heard.

item.title: Asif Mahmud demands arrest, neutral probe into Radda centre vandalism
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain on Sunday demanded the immediate arrest of those involved in the attack, vandalism and looting at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in the capital’s Mirpur area and called for a neutral investigation into the incident.
He visited the health centre around noon with party leaders and activists, inspecting the sections damaged in the vandalism and looting.
Asif spoke with patients who were still receiving treatment at the facility and demanded that the damaged centre be rebuilt and health services restored as soon as possible.
During the visit, NCP activists removed a signboard of a shopkeepers' co-operatives society, which was put up in front of the centre.
Speaking after the inspection, Asif said the facility had long been providing essential maternal and child healthcare services, including vaccination.
“Such destruction of a healthcare facility is completely unacceptable,” he said.
He said medicines, vaccines, injections and medical equipment were also looted from the centre.
The NCP leader alleged that the incident was not isolated and involved a BNP lawmaker, a city corporation administrator and local police, describing it as an “organized crime” and “state-sponsored looting.”
He further alleged that police were present at the scene when the vandalism began but left the spot, returning only after the incident ended.
Asif demanded action against those involved in the attack as well as those accused of negligence of duty.
He said the Radda clinic will not be allowed to be grabbed, adding that health workers will try to keep maternal and child healthcare services running even amid the debris.

item.title: Youth detained in front of PM's residence in Gulshan
item.description:
Police detained a youth near the prime minister’s residence in Gulshan, Dhaka, around 12pm on Sunday.
The detained youth has been identified as Md Shakil Mia, son of Md Abdur Rahim of Karati village in Tarail upazila of Kishoreganj district.
Sub-Inspector (SI) Shakhawat Hossain, the on-duty officer at Gulshan police station, said security personnel became suspicious of Shakil as he was roaming around the area near the prime minister’s residence.
He said Shakil could not provide proper answers when questioned by the security personnel.
As his statements were incoherent, security personnel detained him and informed the Gulshan police station. Police later went to the spot and took him to the police station.
SI Shakhawat Hossain said legal action against Shakil was in process.

Jahangir was attached to the Central Reserve Office of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Headquarters and Administration Department on Saturday afternoon, according to a DMP order.
The order, signed by DMP Deputy Commissioner (Headquarters and Administration) Md Shahriar Ali, was issued on Saturday and came to light on Sunday.
The move came two days after a group of people allegedly attacked the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1 on Thursday night, vandalising the facility and looting valuables, according to police.
DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed visited the centre on Saturday and said police were investigating whether there had been any negligence or failure on their part.
The DMP subsequently formed a committee to investigate the incident and asked it to submit its report within a day.

item.title: BB warns against 22 unauthorized online payment platforms
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank on Sunday issued a public warning notice identifying 22 unlicensed online payment platforms operating in the country and urging the public to refrain from using or participating in their activities.
According to the central bank's Payment Systems Supervision Department, providing payment services or operating a payment system without a valid license from Bangladesh Bank violates Section 4(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, and is punishable under Section 37(1) of the same act.
The department identified the following 22 platforms providing payment aggregator services without statutory approval: BohudurPay, ZiniPay, PayTiller, BengaliPay, Payora BD, SohojPay BD, EasyPayWay, AK Pay, BD PAY, ShajgarPay, AsthaPay/CPay, UddoktaPay, Walletmix, BttPay, Easy Pay Automation, UniquePay BD, BD AUTO PAY, RH Pay BD, EzePay, AutoPay Ltd, Biswasto, and PipraPay.
The central bank advised all individuals, institutions, and businesses to refrain from conducting transactions with or engaging in the operations of these unlicensed payment aggregators to avoid legal penalties and financial risks.
Regulatory actions leading up to this notice have targeted unauthorized digital apps and platforms involved in high-interest online micro-lending, illegal gambling, and financial fraud.
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) and Bangladesh Bank routinely instruct commercial banks and mobile financial services (MFS) to suspend transaction channels for unauthorized platforms that bypass central bank supervision, endanger consumer data, or engage in predatory lending practices.
In July 2024, the Parliament passed the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, significantly strengthening Bangladesh Bank's statutory authority to oversee non-bank digital financial services.
Under Section 4(2) and Section 15(2) of the Act, operating any payment platform, digital wallet, or online transaction gateway without explicit authorization from Bangladesh Bank is illegal.
The law introduced strict penalties under Section 37(1), declaring unlicensed financial operations a cognizable, non-bailable offense punishable by imprisonment, steep fines, or both.
Certain platforms listed in the notice had previously faced regulatory action. For instance, Bangladesh Bank officially canceled the Payment System Operator (PSO) license of Walletmix Limited in November 2023 after detecting unauthorized and illegal financial transactions that violated regulatory terms.
Despite losing its license, platforms attempting to operate or offer payment aggregator tools without authorization remain subject to enforcement.
The Payment Systems Supervision Department launched these sweeps to mitigate systemic risks in the digital ecosystem.
Unregistered payment aggregators and gateways often lack mandatory Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) safeguards, exposing consumers and merchants to risk of financial loss, delayed settlements, data breaches, and illegal fund diversion.

item.title: Standard Chartered Bangladesh, ICAB unveil priority banking for chartered accountants
item.description:
Standard Chartered Bangladesh has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with The Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB) to introduce an exclusive Priority Banking proposition for eligible ICAB members.
Chartered Accountants play a vital role in ensuring good governance, transparency, sustainable growth and bring positive changes to the economy.
Designed to recognize the contribution of Chartered Accountants, this proposition brings together a suite of customized financial and lifestyle benefits for this esteemed professional community.
Subject to applicable terms and conditions, eligible Chartered Accountants can now enjoy a range of preferential banking and financing solutions, including savings on ICAB membership and practitioner fees, cashback and fee waivers on selected products, curated lifestyle and travel privileges, along complimentary supplementary debit cards.
Under this partnership, eligible ICAB members will also have access to Standard Chartered’s broader Priority Banking proposition, including dedicated Relationship Manager support, access to Bancassurance solutions, and Islamic Banking solutions through Standard Chartered Saadiq.
Enamul Huque, CEO Officer, Standard Chartered Bangladesh, said: “Chartered Accountants are an esteemed group of professionals who play a critical role in ensuring good governance and transparency and in safeguarding the business, and policy framework; not only in Bangladesh, but across the world. Our partnership with ICAB recognizes this important contribution. Through this proposition, we aim to offer them convenience, meaningful value and a tailored banking experience in managing their personal finances.”
Sabbir Ahmed, president, ICAB, said: “Delivering value to our members remains an important priority for ICAB. We welcome this collaboration with Standard Chartered, which brings together benefits that address both the professional and personal financial needs of Chartered Accountants. The banking and financing benefits will help members manage their financial priorities with greater flexibility. We look forward to our members benefiting from this partnership and making full use of the proposition.”
The MoU was signed by Enamul Huque, chief executive officer, Standard Chartered Bangladesh and Sabbir Ahmed, president, ICAB.
Senior representatives from both organizations were also present at the ceremony.

item.title: JCI Dhaka Sparks convenes 3rd general members' meeting 2026
item.description:
JCI Dhaka Sparks convened its 3rd General Members' Meeting (GMM) of 2026 on September 26 at the Sirajul Alam Khan Centre and Research Institute in Dhaka.
Local President Raihan Ahmed Dip chaired the assembly, which gathered over 75% of the board of directors alongside national leaders and visiting chapter presidents.
A primary highlight of the meeting was the official launch of the "Green Village" climate initiative.
Presented by director Sahaduzzaman Shrabon, the project aims to tackle deforestation and biomass loss in the Chittagong Division by replacing traditional firewood cookstoves with IoT-enabled eCook Induction Stoves from clean-tech partner ATEC.
Real-time carbon reduction data from the stoves will be verified under Gold Standard accreditation standards.
Local President Raihan Ahmed Dip announced a national Memorandum of Understanding with Hajj with Ayesha, granting all active JCI Bangladesh members a minimum 10% discount on administrative and service fees, as well as special package and ticket privileges.
Earlier, the chapter co-organized a training session on JCI Discover and JCI Explore alongside JCI Dhaka Astral and JCI Dhaka Young.
Conducted by NEVP Shahmina Isha Mannan, the session saw over 40 young leaders complete their core modules.
Six new members were inducted into the chapter: Mir Sadman Ali, Dr. Nazmun Nahar Hafsa, Fatema Tuz Zannat Bristy, Md. Samiul Haque, Tasnuva Rahman Nishim (Opshori), and Abrar Farhan Zaman.
Exceptional performance was recognized with Member of the Month crests presented to ASM Mosabbir Tanim (July), Tasnuva Rahman Nishim (August), and Moumita Siddika (September).
Special recognition was also given to past local president senator Noor E Alam Bhuiyan.
Activity and treasury reports were adopted, covering past projects such as Fight the Bite and PASC 2026.
Members were encouraged to prepare for upcoming events, including the 2026 TOYP Banquet at Radisson Blu Water Garden Hotel on October 17 and the 2026 JCI World Congress in Clark, Philippines, from November 11–15.

item.title: NRB Bank, MetLife renew partnership for 8th consecutive year
item.description:
NRB Bank PLC has renewed its partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth consecutive year to provide enhanced insurance protection benefits for eligible credit cardholders.
Under the agreement, the bank's eligible credit cardholders will receive insurance coverage designed to help settle the outstanding balance on their credit cards in the event of death or permanent disability, subject to policy terms and conditions.
Eligible cardholders will also be entitled to an In-Hospital Cash Benefit for each hospitalization, helping them manage medical expenses during treatment and recovery.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, and Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, has signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, said: "Our customers expect banking services that add meaningful value to their everyday lives. Our partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth year will allow eligible credit cardholders to continue benefiting from insurance protection designed to support them and their families during difficult and unexpected situations."
Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, said: "Financial protection can make an important difference during an unexpected health crisis or other unforeseen event. By continuing our partnership with NRB Bank PLC, we aim to provide impactful insurance benefits that can help reduce financial worries and support greater peace of mind."
NRB Bank is one of the leading providers of card issuance and digital financial services in Bangladesh.
The bank serves customers through multiple channels, including digital banking, branch banking, agent banking, and internet banking, and offers a diversified range of modern, technology-driven banking products and services to meet customers' evolving needs.
MetLife Bangladesh, which has been operating in the country since 1952, currently serves more than one million individual customers and over 900 corporate clients.
The company continues to maintain its leadership position among life insurers in Bangladesh in claims settlement, paying Tk2,853 crore in claims in 2025 and Tk1,384 crore during the first six months of 2026, the highest claims payouts in the industry for the respective periods.
MetLife Bangladesh also maintained a claims settlement ratio of 98% in 2025, one of the highest in the industry.
Senior officials from NRB Bank PLC and MetLife Bangladesh attended the signing ceremony.

item.title: UCB’s ARFL wins ‘Project of the Year’ award for digital innovation
item.description:
United Commercial Bank PLC (UCB) has achieved a significant milestone in its digital transformation journey as its Agri Rural Fast Loan (ARFL) initiative has been named Champion Project of the Year, Information Technology (Medium Category) at the Bangladesh Project Management Symposium & Awards 2026.
The event was recently organized by the Project Management Institute (PMI), Bangladesh Chapter, at a hotel in the capital.
